transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-22 16:00 PDT / Duration: ~42 minutes / Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Thompson (BrightWave Head of ML), Ravi Shah (BrightWave DevOps), Elena Garcia (BrightWave Security)

00:00 Lena Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — happy Thursday. quick check in, we wanted to run through onboarding progress, access stuff, and the initial env readouts Samir had from the perf tests. Maya, want to kick us off with where you are?

00:18 Maya Thompson: Yeah thanks Lena, so on our side we finished the staging VPC config yesterday. we have 3 subnets open for the pilot, and Ravi's working on the peering request. we haven't granted the service account yet, just waiting on the final pw policies from security.

00:34 Ravi Shah: Correct, I'm provisioning the peering but need the Redwood account IDs and a couple of firewall rules confirmed — e g, outbound 443 and the protobuf port 5100 we saw in the doc.

00:49 Samir Patel: Right yeah for the test harness we use 443 mostly, but the agent-to-runtime comms can hit the 5100-ish port depending on routing. If you can't open that we can tunnel over 443 but prefer direct.

01:06 Elena Garcia: Quick security note — we need KMS workflow details. do you support CMKs? and is there any HSM integration for key custody? we also want audit log retention details (how long, and S3 vs retained in your console).

01:28 Samir Patel: We support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations and we have an HSM-backed option for Private deployments; hosted has envelope encryption by default. Audit logs can be exported to your S3 or to our console; retention varies by plan, but we'll send the SOC2 docs.

01:45 Lena Ortiz: We'll put those in tonight's follow-up. Samir, you had some perf numbers from the initial run?

02:00 Samir Patel: Yep, ran the first smoke with their sample dataset — roughly 2k prompts over 10 minutes. average latency was fine ~150ms token-level for the short prompts, but p95/p99 spiked during bursts, p99 reached ~1.4s per request. CPU on the host stayed low but GPU kernel queueing increased. I suspect KV cache warmup and batching policy might need tuning.

02:25 Maya Thompson: Hmm p99 at 1.4s is higher than we'd like — our SLA target for the product is 500ms end-to-end for a typical conversational step.

02:38 Samir Patel: Totally understandable. Two levers: reduce batch wait (smaller windows) or enable more aggressive KV cache/use prefix caching given you have a lot of repeated prefixes. Also we can try an int8 quantized variant we have in the catalog — it's faster on throughput but may need eval for any quality delta.

02:58 Ravi Shah: If we move to quantized, is there any change in the memory footprint that would affect node sizing? we have a cluster of g4dn-equivalent and don't want to underprovision.

03:12 Samir Patel: Good question — quantized models typically reduce VRAM by 30-40% depending on the recipe. For your sample seq lengths (most requests 128 tokens or less) you could get 1.5x more concurrency on the same instance, which might reduce p99. We'll run a quant test and give you the memory/throughput chart.

03:33 Elena Garcia: also need to confirm data residency — any logs containing PII get routed off-prem? we need assurance that training data isn't retained.

03:46 Lena Ortiz: By default logs are tenant-separated and we purge raw transcripts per your retention settings; for Private deployments you control retention. We'll share the data flow diagram and retention configs in the security packet.

04:02 Maya Thompson: Great. Any blocker on the account IDs for peering?

04:08 Ravi Shah: I need the Redwood VPC account IDs — Luca from infra asked for explicit list. Lena can you resend those? last doc I have looked like placeholders.

04:20 Lena Ortiz: Yup — I'll resend the exact account IDs and the CIDR ranges for peering in the follow-up email tonight.

04:27 Samir Patel: On the perf side, I also noted that when we hit burst traffic the autoscaler didn't spin up as fast because our test didn't trigger the scaling queue threshold. For the pilot I'll propose a lower threshold and a modest burst pool for the first two weeks. That should keep tail latency lower for sudden spikes.

04:49 Maya Thompson: Is there a cost implication for the burst pool? we have a tight budget for the proof of concept.

04:54 Lena Ortiz: There is incremental cost — typically it's billed as reserved capacity plus small burst usage. I'll include a pricing estimate for a minimal burst cap in the doc we send tomorrow.

05:05 Ravi Shah: For the peering: our infra team prefers to do IAM-based cross-account roles rather than sharing keys — does Redwood support cross-account role for the service account?

05:18 Samir Patel: Yes we support cross-account IAM roles for Dedicated and Private. For hosted we can do a service-account + scoped token approach. We'll include the recommended pattern per your deployment choice.

05:32 Elena Garcia: Regarding SOC2, can you provide the last audit date and whether you support SCAP/IDS integration? Also need to know if your console supports SAML SSO and RBAC granular roles.

05:46 Lena Ortiz: Yes to SAML SSO and RBAC — we'll send a matrix of supported auth flows. SOC2 last audit was Q1 2026. Samir will attach the report and our network diagram.

06:00 Samir Patel: One more data point on the initial log set — we saw a small number of malformed requests that bumped the error rate. I suspect it's from their test harness' header serialization; Ravi, can you check the client side?

06:12 Ravi Shah: I'll verify, we did build an adapter that serializes a couple header fields — I'll triple-check for the next run.

06:20 Maya Thompson: For the perf benchmark next week, we want the test to simulate 95th percentile user behaviour, not uniform traffic — so ramp and burst patterns. can Redwood's test harness simulate that?

06:32 Samir Patel: Absolutely, our harness can run configurable arrival patterns (poisson, burst, ramp). we'll set up a script that mirrors your production traces if you can provide a sample distribution.

06:45 Maya Thompson: We'll share a week's production trace (anonymized) by EOD Friday.

06:52 Lena Ortiz: Good. Let's talk timeline: if Ravi can get peering and the service account by Friday, Samir can run quant test and a tuned run early next week and we can schedule the 10k prompt perf benchmark for Tuesday 2026-04-28. Sound okay?

07:10 Ravi Shah: Yes that's workable. I'll aim to have peering done by Friday afternoon.

07:18 Elena Garcia: One more quick ask — can Redwood sign a short-term DPA for the pilot? our legal wants a scoped DPA for 60 days.

07:26 Lena Ortiz: We can do a pilot DPA, yes. I'll loop in our legal and share the template.

07:33 Samir Patel: For tuning notes: recommend enabling prefix caching for the conversational flows, batch wait set to 12ms to reduce p99 without impacting average much, and enable KV-cache warmup for known session IDs in the test. I'll include the config snippet.

07:50 Maya Thompson: That batching tweak sounds promising. are there risks to quality with smaller batch sizes?

08:00 Samir Patel: Slightly more variance in sampling for very small batches but we've not seen quality regressions at the sizes we're proposing. quantization needs a careful eval — I'll run a small A/B internal test and share examples.

08:18 Lena Ortiz: OK let's capture action items — Ravi will share peering + grant service account, Samir to run quant and tuned perf, Lena to send pricing and security docs, Elena to list compliance asks. We'll reconvene after the benchmark.

08:35 Maya Thompson: sounds good, thx. Any other questions?

08:40 Elena Garcia: none here.

08:43 Lena Ortiz: thanks everyone. I'll send notes and the account IDs after this call and Samir will post the perf logs once the runs complete. Talk next week.

Meeting end.
